title: Dual-Format Heading Extraction for HTML & Markdown Reports
description: This tour walks through the CLI changes made to support HTML-format library reports in the `hlx library show` command. Previously, the heading extraction regex only matched Markdown headings (`# Title`). Since reports are switching to HTML format, `src/library/show.ts` was updated to try an HTML heading regex first and fall back to the original Markdown regex. No new runtime dependencies were added (the CLI has zero by design). The local `LibraryItemDetail` type was also extended with an optional `filePath` field to align with the updated server API response.

steps.description:
This file is the only format-dependent code in the CLI. The `hlx library show` command parses report content line-by-line to extract headings and annotate them with comment counts. Before this change, only Markdown headings (`# Heading`) were recognized. With reports moving to HTML, headings now look like `

Section Title

`. The fix: add an HTML heading regex that runs first, with the original Markdown regex as a fallback. This preserves full backward compatibility with existing Markdown reports.
steps.title: Overview: What Changed and Why

steps.description: The local `LibraryItemDetail` type mirrors the shape of the server API response. The server (helix-global-server) now includes a `filePath` field in the library item payload. Adding `filePath?: string | null` here as an optional field is strictly backward-compatible — existing Markdown report responses that omit `filePath` continue to work without any changes to downstream consumers. This field can be used for format detection in the future, but the primary detection method is the content-level HTML regex match.
steps.title: L1: Extend Local Type with filePath

steps.description: This is the core of the change. The regex `/<h([1-6])(?:\s+[^>]*?id="([^"]*)"[^>]*)?>(.+?)<\/h\1>/i` is tried first on each line. It captures three groups: (1) heading level 1–6, (2) the `id` attribute value when present, and (3) the raw inner content. Nested HTML tags inside the heading (e.g., `<strong>`) are stripped via `.replace(/<[^>]+>/g, '')` to produce clean display text. When an `id` attribute is present it is used directly as the anchor slug, falling back to `slugify(rawText)` only when absent. A `continue` statement after a successful match prevents the same line from being re-evaluated by the Markdown regex.
steps.title: L2: HTML Heading Regex (Primary Pattern)

steps.description: After a line is matched and processed as an HTML heading, `continue` skips the rest of the loop body for that line. This is the key guard that ensures a single line cannot be double-processed by both the HTML and Markdown patterns. Without this, an HTML heading line would fall through to the Markdown regex, fail to match, and be silently skipped — but the `continue` makes the control flow explicit and safe.
steps.title: Guard: continue After HTML Match

steps.description: The original Markdown heading regex `/^(#{1,6})\s+(.+)$/` is completely unchanged from the pre-implementation code. It only executes for lines that did not match the HTML pattern above. This guarantees that all existing Markdown reports continue to render identically. Both the HTML and Markdown branches produce output in the same format — heading level indicator plus slug annotation — so the rest of the display logic requires no changes. The zero-new-dependencies constraint is fully respected: no HTML parsing library was introduced.
steps.title: L2: Markdown Heading Regex (Fallback, Unchanged)

steps.description: The CLI's `slugify()` function (lines 15–22) is used as a fallback anchor generator when an HTML heading lacks an explicit `id` attribute. Note that this function differs slightly from the client-side `slugify()` (different regex steps, no 60-character truncation). This is a pre-existing difference and only affects headings without an `id` attribute. For HTML headings generated by the updated agent prompts, the `id` attribute is always present and extracted directly, so this fallback path is rarely exercised in practice. No change was needed here.
steps.title: Supporting: slugify() Fallback

steps.description: All major code paths remain clean after this change. (1) HTML reports: HTML regex matches first, extracts level + id + text, `continue` prevents double-processing, comment annotations work identically. (2) Markdown reports: HTML regex does not match, Markdown fallback runs unchanged, full backward compatibility preserved. (3) Comment commands (`comments-list.ts`, `comments-post.ts`): completely format-agnostic — they operate on anchor strings passed via `--section` flag and were not touched. TypeScript compilation (`npx tsc --noEmit`) passes with zero errors. Zero new runtime dependencies added.
steps.title: Summary: Clean Code Paths Confirmed
